# GuiExpert Table (@guiexpert/table)

> A framework-agnostic, high-performance data grid for the browser: virtual scrolling in both directions (millions of
> rows), zero runtime dependencies, full control over HTML and CSS, MIT-licensed (also for commercial use). One core
> (`@guiexpert/table`, plain TypeScript) with wrappers for Angular 14–22, React, Preact, Vue 3, Svelte 4/5, Solid and a
> Web Component.

This file is a usage guide for AI assistants and people: **recipes** (the shortest correct code for typical tasks),
**pitfalls** (symptom → cause → fix), quick answers and a feature reference. Every `ts` snippet below is compiled
against the real API (`pnpm check:llms`); names are exact – including the misspelled ones (`showCheckboxWihoutExtraColumn`,
`isHeaderVisibe`, `emmitDataKey`, `createCoverGrisDefaultOptions`), do not "correct" them. If something is not in this
file or in [instructions.md](https://github.com/guiexperttable/mono/blob/main/instructions.md), do not invent it –
the code wins (API: https://gui.expert/api).

## Packages

- `@guiexpert/table` – the core (plain JS/TS). Stylesheet `@guiexpert/table/css/main.css`.
- `@guiexpert/react-table`, `@guiexpert/preact-table`, `@guiexpert/solid-table`, `@guiexpert/svelte-table` (Svelte 4 and 5),
  `@guiexpert/vue3-table`, `@guiexpert/webcomponent-table` – wrappers with the same version as the core (1.1.x / Svelte 5.1.x).
- `@guiexpert/angular-table@NN.x` – one build per Angular major 14 … 22 (`@guiexpert/angular-table@22` for Angular 22);
  Angular 22+ also has `TableSignalComponent` (`<guiexpert-table-signal>`).
- `@guiexpert/demo-table-models` – demo data and model factories (not needed in apps).

Repository: https://github.com/guiexperttable/mono · License: MIT (current releases; future releases may be
dual-licensed, see https://gui.expert/license/).

## How to use – recipes

Concepts in one paragraph: a **table model** (`TableModelIf`, built by `TableFactory.createTableModel(...)`) holds three
**area models** (header, body, footer) and the column definitions; **table options** (`TableOptionsIf`, always
`{ ...new TableOptions(), ... }`) switch features on; a **`TableScope`** renders the model into a host `div` and gives you
the **`TableApi`** (`tableScope.getApi()`, in wrappers the `tableReady` event). Events go to an **`EventListenerIf`**
(extend `EventAdapter`). Indices in events and API calls are **display indices** (after filtering and sorting).

### R1 – First table (plain TypeScript)

How do I show an array of objects?

```ts
import "@guiexpert/table/css/main.css";               // or <link> to https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@guiexpert/table/css/main.css
import { EventAdapter, SimpleDomService, TableFactory, TableOptions, TableScope } from "@guiexpert/table";

interface Order { id: number; customer: string; total: number }
const orders: Order[] = [{ id: 1, customer: "Smith & Co", total: 120.5 }, { id: 2, customer: "Jones", total: 99 }];

const host = document.querySelector<HTMLDivElement>(".table-div")!;   // needs a fixed height, e.g. height: 500px
const tableModel = TableFactory.createTableModel({ rows: orders, properties: ["id", "customer", "total"] });
const tableOptions = { ...new TableOptions(), hoverColumnVisible: false };
const tableScope = new TableScope(host, tableModel, new SimpleDomService(), tableOptions, new EventAdapter());
tableScope.firstInit();
const tableApi = tableScope.getApi();
```

- The host `div` **must have a height** (`.table-div { height: 500px }` or a flex/grid parent) – otherwise nothing is visible.
- Values are shown as text by default (no renderer needed). Column labels, widths, renderers:
  `columnDefs: [ColumnDef.create({ property: "total", headerLabel: "Total", width: px120 })]`
  instead of `properties`. Sizes: `px0 … px500` or `new Size(2, "weight")` / `new Size(30, "%")`.
- Remove or replace the table: `tableApi.destroy()` first (wrappers do it themselves). → instructions.md 2, 4.1, 5.1–5.2

### R2 – The same table in a framework (and how to get the TableApi)

Every wrapper takes `tableModel` + `tableOptions` and reports the `TableApi` once (`tableReady`). **A new model or
options object re-creates the table** (state, scroll position, selection gone) – create them once (outside the
component, `useMemo`, a constant / `shallowRef`, a class field) and change data through the `TableApi`.

```tsx
// React (Preact and Solid: same props)
import { GuiexpertTable } from "@guiexpert/react-table";
import { GeMouseEvent, TableApi, TableFactory, TableOptions } from "@guiexpert/table";
import { useMemo, useRef } from "react";

export function Orders({ orders }: { orders: { id: number; total: number }[] }) {
  const api = useRef<TableApi>();
  const tableModel = useMemo(() => TableFactory.createTableModel({ rows: orders, properties: ["id", "total"] }), [orders]);
  const tableOptions = useMemo(() => new TableOptions(), []);
  return <div className="table-div">
    <GuiexpertTable tableModel={tableModel} tableOptions={tableOptions}
      tableReady={(a: TableApi) => api.current = a}
      mouseClicked={(e: GeMouseEvent) => console.log(e.rowIndex)} />
  </div>;
}
```

- Callback props may be inline functions – the wrapper always calls the latest one; only `tableModel`/`tableOptions`
  identity matters. React/Preact/Solid clicks are not debounced. The component fills its parent (100 % × 100 %): give
  the parent a height.
- **Vue 3**: `<GuiexpertTable :tableModel :tableOptions @tableReady="api = $event" @mouseClicked="…" />`; model as a
  constant or `shallowRef` (a deep `ref()` wraps it in a proxy). Clicks are debounced (`debounceMouseClickDelay`, 150 ms, `0` = immediate).
- **Angular** (14–22): `<guiexpert-table [tableModel]="model" [tableOptions]="options" (tableReady)="api = $event" (mouseClicked)="…">`
  (`TableComponent`, standalone; `(mouseDraggingEnded)`, `(contextMenu)` – not `(contextmenu)`). **Angular 22+**:
  `<guiexpert-table-signal [tableModel]="model" [(tableApi)]="api" />` with `api = signal<TableApi | undefined>(undefined)`
  (no `tableReady`, zoneless). Guide: `packages/angular-table/instructions.md`.
- **Svelte**: `<GuiexpertTable {tableModel} {tableOptions} on:tableReady={e => api = e.detail} />` or (runes)
  `onTableReady={a => api = a}`.
- **Web Component**: `customElements.define("guiexpert-table", GuiexpertTable)` yourself, then
  `el.data = new TableModelAndOptions(tableModel, tableOptions)`; events are `CustomEvent`s on the element (`e.detail`).
  → instructions.md 4.2–4.8

### R3 – Mouse events (click, double click, context menu)

```ts
import { EventAdapter, GeMouseEvent, SimpleDomService, TableFactory, TableOptions, TableScope } from "@guiexpert/table";

interface Order { id: number; customer: string }
declare const host: HTMLDivElement;
declare const orders: Order[];

const listener = new EventAdapter();
listener.onMouseClicked = (evt: GeMouseEvent) => {
  if (evt.areaIdent !== "body") return;                                   // "header" | "body" | "footer"
  const order = tableApi.getBodyModel().getRowByIndex(evt.rowIndex) as Order; // the DISPLAYED row (filter/sort applied)
  if (evt.clickCount === 2) console.log("open", order.id); else console.log("select", order.id);
};
listener.onContextmenu = (evt: GeMouseEvent) => {
  evt.originalEvent?.preventDefault();                                    // no browser menu – show your own menu
  console.log("menu at", evt.originalEvent?.clientX, evt.originalEvent?.clientY, "row", evt.rowIndex);
};
const tableModel = TableFactory.createTableModel({ rows: orders, properties: ["id", "customer"] });
const tableScope = new TableScope(host, tableModel, new SimpleDomService(), new TableOptions(), listener);
tableScope.firstInit();
const tableApi = tableScope.getApi();
const unsubscribe = tableApi.subscribe({ onMouseClicked: e => console.log("second listener", e.rowIndex) });
```

- `rowIndex`/`columnIndex` are display/model indices – never use `orders[evt.rowIndex]` (wrong after sorting or
  filtering). `getRowByIndex()` returns `any` (cast it); `undefined` outside the rows. Column by name:
  `tableApi.getColumnIndex("customer")`. Without a selection model a click still fires `onMouseClicked` and moves the
  focus frame – it only selects nothing.
- A double click arrives as a click with `clickCount: 1`, then one with `clickCount: 2`. On a header cell a double click
  sorts (sortable columns), on an editable body cell it opens the editor.
- Since 1.1.108 a click is reported even if your code renders between `mousedown` and `mouseup` (live data).
- There is no built-in context menu – `onContextmenu` + your own HTML. `onMouseMoved` fires per mouse move (keep it cheap).
  → instructions.md 6.5, training "events-and-context-menu"

### R4 – Keyboard: built-in keys and your own keys

Built in (WAI-ARIA grid): arrows, Home/End, Ctrl/⌘+Home/End, Page Up/Down, Enter (`ACTIVATE_CELL`), F2 (edit),
Ctrl/⌘+A, Ctrl/⌘+C – macOS uses ⌘. There is **no keyboard event in `EventListenerIf`**: react to your own keys with a
`keydown` listener on the host and read the focused cell with `getActiveCell()`.

```ts
import { ShortcutActionIdMapping, TableApi, TableOptions, TableOptionsIf } from "@guiexpert/table";

declare const host: HTMLDivElement;      // the element you passed to TableScope (in wrappers: the component's element)
declare const tableApi: TableApi;

host.addEventListener("keydown", evt => {          // the Delete key removes the focused row
  if (evt.key !== "Delete") return;
  const cell = tableApi.getActiveCell();          // [row, column] of the focused body cell, or undefined
  if (!cell) return;
  const row = tableApi.getBodyModel().getRowByIndex(cell[0]);
  tableApi.removeRows([row]);
  tableApi.repaintHard();
});

const shortcutActionIdMapping: ShortcutActionIdMapping = { "ctrl c": "COPY_2_CLIPBOARD", "f2": "START_EDITING" };
const tableOptions: TableOptionsIf = { ...new TableOptions(), shortcutActionIdMapping }; // spellings are harmonized
tableApi.triggerAction("NAVIGATE_DOWN");                                                // run an action from code
```

- Every table has a cell focus by default (an own `FocusModel("cell")`): a click or the arrow keys move it, so
  `getActiveCell()` works without configuration. To keep a reference, pass `getFocusModel: () => focusModel`
  (`new FocusModel("cell")`) and read `focusModel.getFocus()`; `onFocusChanged` reports moves.
- Your `keydown` listener and the table's own handler both run (both listen on the host); the table does not stop the
  event. Enter also triggers the built-in `ACTIVATE_CELL` (toggles a row checkbox / tree node, else nothing); with
  `editing` (Excel-style) Delete also clears the selected cells – remap or disable those keys
  (`shortcutActionIdMapping`, `shortcutActionsDisabled: true` switches all built-in keys off).
- `removeRows(rows, predicate?)` works on a `TableFactory.createTableModel({ rows })` body: O(n) (filters all rows into a
  new array), returns nothing and does not repaint – call `repaintHard()`. Selection and focus indices are not
  adjusted (the focus stays at the same index = the next row) – clear or re-set the selection afterwards.
- Your own shortcut that the browser also uses (Ctrl/⌘+S): `evt.preventDefault()` in your `keydown` listener; check
  `evt.ctrlKey || evt.metaKey` (macOS).
- The table is **one tab stop**; controls inside cells must have `tabindex="-1"`.
  → instructions.md 6.4, 6.14

### R5 – Row selection and the selected rows

The default selection type is `"none"` – nothing is selected until you pass a selection model.

```ts
import { CellRange, SelectionModel, TableApi, TableOptions, TableOptionsIf } from "@guiexpert/table";

interface Order { id: number; total: number }
declare const tableApi: TableApi;

const selectionModel = new SelectionModel("row", "multi");   // "none" | "cell" | "row" | "column" | "range"; "single" | "multi"
const tableOptions: TableOptionsIf = { ...new TableOptions(), getSelectionModel: () => selectionModel };

function selectedOrders(): Order[] {                           // the selected row OBJECTS
  const body = tableApi.getBodyModel();
  return selectionModel.getMergedRowIndices(body.getRowCount()).map(i => body.getRowByIndex(i) as Order);
}
const sumOfSelected = () => selectedOrders().reduce((sum, o) => sum + o.total, 0);

selectionModel.addSelection(CellRange.singleRow(3));          // select from code (repaint to show it)
tableApi.repaint();
tableApi.clearSelection();                                     // clears and repaints
```

- React to changes: `listener.onSelectionChanged = (sm: SelectionModelIf) => …` (wrappers: `selectionChanged`) – fires
  after mouse and keyboard changes, the model is already up to date (reading your own `selectionModel` is the same).
  Mouse: click, Shift+click (range), Ctrl/⌘+click (toggle), drag (`"range"`). Focus (the frame) ≠ selection.
- `getMergedRowIndices()` returns a new sorted array of display indices – O(selected rows); for "select all" on huge
  tables check `selectionModel.isAllSelected()` first.
- `tableApi.getSelectionAggregates()` = count/sum/avg/min/max of the selected **numeric cells** (all columns) – for one
  column use the row objects as above.
- Indices: `externalFilterChanged()` and `setRows()` clear the selection; sorting keeps the indices (not the rows).
  `appendRows()` keeps the selection at its rows. Restore by row id: state API part `selection` (`getState`/`applyState`).
- Checkboxes instead: `TableFactory.createTableModel({ rows, properties, rowCheckboxVisible: true })` + `onCheckboxChanged`.
  → instructions.md 6.4, 6.6, 6.11

### R6 – Change data: the right update

| What changed | Call | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| a few cell values | `tableApi.updateCells([new TableCellUpdateEvent("body", row, col, value, cssClasses?)])` | only these cells |
| values inside your row objects (same row count) | `tableApi.repaint()` | one render |
| row count or row heights (own area model) | `tableApi.repaintHard()` / `repaintHard({ py })` | one render |
| rows keep coming (log, stream) | `tableApi.appendRows(rows, { follow, maxRows })` (R7) | O(k), one render |
| a new data set | `tableApi.setRows(rows)` + `tableApi.repaintHard()` (+ `externalFilterChanged()` with a filter) | O(n) |
| new columns / structure | a new table model | rebuild – avoid for data |

```ts
import { TableApi, TableCellUpdateEvent } from "@guiexpert/table";

declare const tableApi: TableApi;
const changes = new Map<number, number>();               // display row → new price, collected from a WebSocket

function flush() {                                       // once per animation frame, not once per message
  const col = tableApi.getColumnIndex("price");
  tableApi.updateCells([...changes].map(([row, price]) =>
    new TableCellUpdateEvent("body", row, col, price, { "ge-table-color-error": price < 0 })));
  changes.clear();
  requestAnimationFrame(flush);
}
requestAnimationFrame(flush);
```

- `updateCells` takes the **displayed** row index and writes into that row object (after sorting/filtering this is not
  the index in your array). A totals footer follows automatically. `updateCells` with a body from
  `createTableModel({ rows })` updates **your** objects – read the old value before the call.
- `cssClasses` (`{ className: boolean }`, optional) adds (`true`) or removes (`false`) classes on the **current** cell
  element only – a flash: it stays until the cell is drawn again (scrolling, a repaint), then it is gone. Set both
  directions on every update (`{ "tick-up": up, "tick-down": !up }`), otherwise an old class stays. Colors that must
  survive scrolling belong into the model (`getCustomClassesAt`, see the heatmap showcases). Your CSS, e.g.
  `.tick-up { color: #15803d } .tick-down { color: #be123c }` (no prefix needed). A ticker:

```ts
import { TableApi, TableCellUpdateEvent } from "@guiexpert/table";

interface Quote { symbol: string; price: number }
declare const tableApi: TableApi;

setInterval(() => {                                       // 50 random prices every 100 ms – one updateCells call
  const col = tableApi.getColumnIndex("price");
  const body = tableApi.getBodyModel();
  const events: TableCellUpdateEvent[] = [];
  for (let n = 0; n < 50; n++) {
    const row = Math.floor(Math.random() * body.getRowCount());   // a displayed row
    const quote = body.getRowByIndex(row) as Quote;
    const price = Math.round(quote.price * (1 + (Math.random() - 0.5) / 50) * 100) / 100;
    const up = price >= quote.price;
    events.push(new TableCellUpdateEvent("body", row, col, price, { "tick-up": up, "tick-down": !up }));
  }
  tableApi.updateCells(events);                            // only these cells are redrawn
}, 100);
```

Showcase "crypto", training chapter "live-data".
  → instructions.md 6.9, 6.13, showcases "fps", "crypto"

### R7 – A rolling log: rows that keep coming (since 1.1.108)

```ts
import { TableApi } from "@guiexpert/table";

interface LogLine { time: string; level: string; text: string }
declare const tableApi: TableApi;
const pending: LogLine[] = [];
let frozen = false, newBelow = 0, scheduled = false;

function onMessage(line: LogLine) {                      // e.g. WebSocket: buffer, append once per frame
  pending.push(line);
  if (!scheduled) { scheduled = true; requestAnimationFrame(flush); }
}
function flush() {
  scheduled = false;
  const result = tableApi.appendRows(pending.splice(0), { follow: frozen ? false : "auto", maxRows: 1_000_000 });
  if (result) newBelow = result.following ? 0 : newBelow + result.shown;   // "+N new lines"
}
function setFrozen(f: boolean) { frozen = f; }            // "Freeze scroll" button
function scrollToEnd() { frozen = false; newBelow = 0; tableApi.repaintHard({ py: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER }); }
```

- `appendRows` (body from `TableFactory.createTableModel({ rows })`): pushes into **your** array (no copy), runs the
  filter only for the new rows, merges them into a sorted view, keeps selection/focus/anchor at their rows, renders once
  – and not at all if only rows below the view came in. `follow: "auto"` = stay at the end if the view was at the end
  (an empty table counts as "at the end"), otherwise keep the first visible row; `false` = always keep the first
  visible row (also at the end, also while the ring buffer drops older rows – unless that row itself leaves); while the
  mouse button is held, the rows under the pointer stay. After `scrollToEnd()` the view is at the end, so `"auto"`
  follows again.
- Result `{ added, shown, removed, following }`: `shown` = new rows that passed the filter (use it for "+N new lines"),
  `removed` = rows dropped by `maxRows`. A body that cannot append (tree, row groups, pivot) → `false`.
- `maxRows`: the oldest rows leave in blocks of ≥ 1 % (row count 99–100 % of `maxRows`). Measured (Chromium, Mac): ~3–4 ms
  per update of 500 rows incl. render, the same for 100,000 and 2,000,000 rows; ~0.5 ms for a reader in the middle.
- Own area model: append yourself (a loop – `push(...lines)` overflows above ~100,000), then
  `tableApi.rowsAppended(count, { follow: "auto", removedAtStart })`.
- Clicks: read the line in the handler (`getRowByIndex(evt.rowIndex)`) – a stored index points to another line after
  the next update. Keys: R4. Pause the intake = keep buffering, call `appendRows` later once.
- Don't: `addRows()` per tick (copies all rows, resets filter and sort order), a new model per tick, `repaintHard()`
  without a position. Showcase "logtail", `apps/table-demo/log-tail.html`. → instructions.md 6.9

### R8 – Millions of rows (own area model)

```ts
import { AreaModel, ColumnDef, TableFactory, px120 } from "@guiexpert/table";

class MillionRows extends AreaModel {                     // values on demand – no object per row
  constructor(private readonly count: number) { super(); this.areaIdent = "body"; }
  override getRowCount(): number { return this.count; }
  override getRowHeight(): number { return 24; }
  override getConstantRowHeight(): number { return 24; }  // all rows equal → O(1) positions
  override getValueAt(row: number, col: number): string { return col === 0 ? String(row) : `cell ${row}/${col}`; }
}
const tableModel = TableFactory.createTableModel({
  bodyAreaModel: new MillionRows(10_000_000),
  columnDefs: ["#", "A", "B"].map((label, i) => new ColumnDef("c" + i, label, px120)),
});
```

- Variable heights: return them from `getRowHeight(i)` and leave out `getConstantRowHeight()` (prefix sums, O(log n)).
  The scroll height comes from the model (since 1.1.107). Showcase "large" (2 million rows). → instructions.md 5.5

### R9 – Sorting and filtering

```ts
import { ColumnDef, TableApi, TableOptions, TableOptionsIf, TrueFn } from "@guiexpert/table";

interface Order { id: number; customer: string; total: number }
declare const tableApi: TableApi;
let search = "";

const columnDefs = [
  ColumnDef.create({ property: "customer", headerLabel: "Customer", sortable: TrueFn }),
  ColumnDef.create({ property: "total", headerLabel: "Total", sortable: TrueFn,
    sortComparator: (a: number, b: number) => a - b }),
];
const tableOptions: TableOptionsIf = {
  ...new TableOptions(),
  externalFilterFunction: (order: Order) => order.customer.toLowerCase().includes(search),
};
function onSearch(text: string) { search = text.toLowerCase(); tableApi.externalFilterChanged(); }
tableApi.sortByColumn("total", "desc");                   // like a double click on the header
```

- The header sorts on **double click** (not single click). After changing data: `tableApi.reSort()`.
- `externalFilterChanged()` filters all rows, clears the selection and scrolls to the top. There is no built-in filter
  UI – build inputs yourself. → instructions.md 6.2, 6.3

### R10 – Own cell renderer

```ts
import { AreaIdent, AreaModelIf, CellRendererIf, ColumnDef, DomServiceIf, RendererCleanupFnType } from "@guiexpert/table";

class StatusRenderer implements CellRendererIf {
  render(cellDiv: HTMLDivElement, rowIndex: number, columnIndex: number, areaIdent: AreaIdent,
         areaModel: AreaModelIf, cellValue: unknown, domService: DomServiceIf): RendererCleanupFnType | undefined {
    const badge = domService.createElement<HTMLSpanElement>("span");
    domService.addClass(badge, "status-" + String(cellValue));
    domService.appendChild(badge, domService.createText(String(cellValue)));  // text – never data in innerHTML
    domService.appendChild(cellDiv, badge);
    return undefined;                                                          // or a cleanup function
  }
}
const column = ColumnDef.create({ property: "status", headerLabel: "Status", bodyRenderer: new StatusRenderer() });
```

- Built in: `NumberCellRenderer`, `ProgressBarCellRenderer`, `StarRatingCellRenderer`, `DateToLocaleDateCellRenderer`,
  `TrueFalseCellRenderer`, `CheckboxCellRenderer`, … Framework components as cells: `ComponentRendererWrapper` (React,
  Preact, Vue, Svelte, Solid), Angular `RenderWrapperFactory.create(MyComponent, cdr)`.
- If you must build HTML: `escapeHtml(value)`. Buttons/inputs in a cell: `tabindex="-1"`. → instructions.md 6.1, 6.14

### R11 – Editing

```ts
import { ColumnDef, EventAdapter, GeModelChangeEvent, TableOptions, TableOptionsIf, TrueFn } from "@guiexpert/table";

const columns = [ColumnDef.create({ property: "qty", headerLabel: "Qty", editable: TrueFn,
  validate: (value: unknown) => typeof value === "number" && value >= 0 ? undefined : "must be ≥ 0" })];
const tableOptions: TableOptionsIf = { ...new TableOptions(), editing: true };   // Excel-style: type over, Enter, Tab, Delete
const listener = new EventAdapter();
listener.onModelChanged = (evt: GeModelChangeEvent) => {
  evt.changes?.forEach(c => console.log(c.property, c.oldValue, "→", c.newValue, "row", c.row));  // save here
};
```

- Without `editing`: double click / F2 opens the classic in-cell editor (`editable`). "Collect, then save":
  `batchEdit: true` + `commitBatchEdit()`. Paste from Excel: `clipboard: true`; undo: `undo: true`.
  → instructions.md 6.7, 6.17, 6.20–6.22

### R12 – Columns: fixed, hidden, width, index

- Fixed columns belong to the **model**: `TableFactory.createTableModel({ rows, properties, fixedLeftColumnCount: 1, fixedRightColumnCount: 1 })`.
- `tableApi.setColumnVisible("total", false)`, `tableApi.setColumnWidth(index, px)`, `tableApi.autoResizeColumns()`,
  one column `tableApi.autoResizeColumn("name")` (since 1.1.110).
- Lock a column for the user: `ColumnDef.create({ …, resizable: false, movable: false })` (since 1.1.110). Save the
  layout when the user drags: R18.
- Row numbers (`rowNumbersVisible: true`), a checkbox column or a row-group column shift all column indices by one –
  always `tableApi.getColumnIndex(property)`. Header groups: `instructions.md` 5.2, demo "headergroup".

### R13 – Look and feel

- CSS variables `--ge-table-*` (`packages/table/css/table-color-vars.css`), dark mode with `<html data-theme="dark">`.
- Hide scroll bars: `.my-table .ge-table-scroll-viewport { scrollbar-width: none; }` (no option needed).
- Right-to-left: `tableOptions.direction: "rtl"` (or `"auto"`). Borders, hover: `verticalBorderVisible`,
  `hoverRowVisible`, `hoverColumnVisible`. → instructions.md 6.12, 6.19

### R14 – Remember the state (sorting, widths, scroll position, selection)

```ts
import { AutoRestoreOptions, TableApi, TableOptions, TableOptionsIf } from "@guiexpert/table";

declare const tableApi: TableApi;
const tableOptions: TableOptionsIf = {
  ...new TableOptions(),
  autoRestoreOptions: {
    ...new AutoRestoreOptions<{ id: number }>(),
    getStorageKeyFn: () => "orders-table",        // REQUIRED – without a key nothing is stored
    getRowId: row => row.id,                      // selection/checked rows by id, not by index
    autoRestoreSortingState: true, autoRestoreColumnLayout: true, autoRestoreScrollPosition: true,
    autoRestoreSelectedState: true,
  },
};
const state = tableApi.getState();                 // JSON for your server; later tableApi.applyState(state)
```

→ instructions.md 6.11

### R15 – Export

`await tableApi.copyToClipboard()` (selection, tab-separated) and `tableApi.downloadExcel("orders.xlsx", "author")`
(own XLSX writer, the **current view**: filtered and sorted rows + header + footer). All rows or other data:
`new ExcelService().downloadExcel(matrix, …)`. → instructions.md 6.10

### R16 – Lifecycle

Plain TS: call `tableApi.destroy()` before you replace the model or remove the host (listeners, ResizeObserver, renderer
cleanups). Wrappers do it on unmount and on a new model/options object. Never create a second `TableScope` on the same
host without destroying the first.

### R17 – Not built in (and how to do it)

- **Filter UI**: inputs of your own + `externalFilterFunction` + `externalFilterChanged()` (R9).
- **Context menu**: `onContextmenu` + your own HTML menu (R3); example `apps/table-demo/spreadsheet.html`.
- **Pagination**: not needed for size (virtual scrolling); if wanted, `setRows(page)` + `repaintHard()`.
- **Server-side row model** (fetch rows on demand): an own `AreaModel` whose `getValueAt` reads a cache and requests
  missing blocks; `repaint()` when a block arrives (R8).
- **Drag between tables**: row drag works inside one table (`rowDrag: true`); between tables use `onRowDragEnd` +
  `rowDragOptions.managed: false` and move the data yourself.

### R18 – Save the column layout when the user resizes or moves a column (since 1.1.110)

```ts
import { EventAdapter } from "@guiexpert/table";
import type { GeColumnMoveEvent, GeColumnResizeEvent, TableApi } from "@guiexpert/table";

declare const tableApi: TableApi;
const listener = new EventAdapter();               // 5th argument of new TableScope(…); wrappers: columnResizeEnd …
listener.onColumnResizeEnd = (evt: GeColumnResizeEvent) => {
  if (evt.type === "end") localStorage.setItem("layout", JSON.stringify(tableApi.getState(["columns"])));
};
listener.onColumnMoveEnd = (evt: GeColumnMoveEvent) => {
  if (evt.moved) localStorage.setItem("layout", JSON.stringify(tableApi.getState(["columns"])));
};
```

Once per drag, after the table applied the change (no `setTimeout`); `type: "cancel"` after Escape; API calls
(`setColumnWidth`, `applyState`, `autoResizeColumns`) report nothing. Double click on the resize handle fits the width
(`source: "dblclick"`; own measurement `tableOptions.columnAutoWidth.getWidth`). Renders of a live table while the
user drags are fine. → instructions.md 6.27

More (short): tree + checkboxes `TreeFactory` (instructions.md 6.6), master/detail `masterDetail` (6.18), row grouping
`RowGroupFactory` (5.6), pivot `PivotFactory` (5.7), calculated columns `valueGetter`/`formula` (5.2, 5.9), spreadsheet
`SpreadsheetFactory.create` (6.25), cover grid (5.10), totals footer `footerAggregates` (5.4), row numbers (5.2).

## Pitfalls

Symptom → cause → fix.

- **The table is empty / invisible** → the host has no height or the CSS is missing → give the host a fixed height and
  load `@guiexpert/table/css/main.css`.
- **The table is rebuilt on every render; selection, scroll position and sorting are lost** → a new model or options
  object per render (inline in JSX/templates, a deep `ref()`, a computed that creates a new object) → create them once;
  change data through the `TableApi` (R6).
- **Clicks select nothing / no `onSelectionChanged`** → selection type defaults to `"none"` → pass
  `getSelectionModel: () => new SelectionModel("row", "multi")`.
- **The wrong row is used after sorting/filtering** → `rowIndex` is the displayed index → `getRowByIndex(rowIndex)`,
  never `myRows[rowIndex]`.
- **The wrong column** → row numbers/checkbox/group column shift indices → `tableApi.getColumnIndex(property)`.
- **Single click on the header does not sort** → it sorts on double click → or `tableApi.sortByColumn(...)`.
- **Selection gone after filtering; view jumps to the top** → `externalFilterChanged()` does that by design → restore via
  the state API (`getState(["selection"])` / `applyState`) with `getRowId`.
- **`repaint()` after adding rows shows nothing new / wrong scroll bar** → the row count changed → `repaintHard()`
  (or `appendRows`).
- **Slow live updates** → a new model, `setRows` or `addRows` per tick → `updateCells` (values) or `appendRows` (new
  rows), once per animation frame.
- **`Maximum call stack size exceeded`** → `array.push(...rows)` with ~100,000+ rows → a `for` loop (or `appendRows`).
- **Clicks lost while the table updates** (before 1.1.108) → a render between `mousedown` and `mouseup` → update to
  1.1.108; older: render only when the visible part changed.
- **Context menu right after creating the table is ignored** → the first 50 ms are swallowed → normal; Angular: use
  `(contextMenu)` – `(contextmenu)` fires twice (also the native event).
- **Clicks arrive late in Angular/Vue** → `debounceMouseClickDelay` (150 ms) → `0` for immediate clicks (a double click
  then also delivers the single click first).
- **Own model with 20 px rows shows a scroll bar / wrong height** (before 1.1.107) → `defaultRowHeights` won → update,
  or set `defaultRowHeights.body` to your height. Since 1.1.107 the model's `getRowHeight()` wins.
- **Shortcut works on Windows, not on the Mac** → checked `ctrlKey` → the table uses ⌘ on macOS; map both or use the
  table's actions.
- **Second tab stop / keyboard focus lost in a cell** → focusable elements in a cell → `tabindex="-1"`.
- **XSS from cell values** → data in `innerHTML` of a renderer → `textContent` / `domService.createText` / `escapeHtml`.
- **State is not stored** → `autoRestoreOptions` without `getStorageKeyFn` (a console warning says so) → add the key.
- **`instanceof AreaModelTree` is false** → two copies of the core in the bundle → `isAreaModelTree(x)`, `isTreeRow(x)`;
  dedupe `@guiexpert/table`.
- **TypeScript: unknown option** → "corrected" a misspelled API → use `showCheckboxWihoutExtraColumn`, `isHeaderVisibe`,
  `emmitDataKey`, `createCoverGrisDefaultOptions` as they are.
- **Own `mousedown`/`mouseup`/`dblclick` listeners on the header** (to save widths, lock a column, fit on double click)
  → the table had no column events before 1.1.110 → `onColumnResizeEnd` / `onColumnMoveEnd` (R18),
  `ColumnDef.resizable: false` / `movable: false`, the built-in double click (`columnAutoWidth`).
- **`AsyncBodyAreaModelObjectArray` cannot be imported** → unfinished, not exported → own `AreaModel` (R8, R17).
- **Invented APIs** – these do NOT exist: `getSelectedRows()`, `onKeyDown`, `api.addRow()`, `api.refresh()`,
  `setData()`, `gridOptions`, `rowData`, `columnDefs` as a table option (it is a model parameter). Use R4–R7.

## Quick answers (FAQ)
Full answers: instructions.md section 6.26 (https://github.com/guiexperttable/mono/blob/main/instructions.md#626-faq--quick-answers).
- Hide the scroll bars: CSS `.my-table .ge-table-scroll-viewport { scrollbar-width: none; }` – the table uses the full width/height, wheel, touch, keyboard and the API still scroll. No table option needed (`overflowY` is only "auto" | "scroll"). Thin/colored: `scrollbar-width: thin; scrollbar-color: …`.
- Scroll bar although all rows fit (own AreaModel): fixed in 1.1.107 – the scroll height comes from the model's `getConstantRowHeight()` / `getRowHeight()`. Older versions: set `defaultRowHeights.body` to the model's row height.
- Rows appended continuously (live log, ticker) and keep the position or follow the end: `tableApi.repaintHard({ py })` – one render pass (since 1.1.107); follow the end with `py: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`.
- Clicks lost while the app renders (live tail, `repaint()`/`repaintHard()` between mousedown and mouseup): fixed in 1.1.108 – the table reports `mouseClicked` (and the double click) for the pressed cell itself, once, with the current index of that row object.
- Rows that keep coming (log, stream, ticker of trades): `tableApi.appendRows(rows, { follow: "auto", maxRows })` (since 1.1.108) – in place, O(k), one render, filter/sort only for new rows, selection/focus stay; freeze = `follow: false`, jump to the end = `repaintHard({ py: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER })`. Own AreaModel: `rowsAppended(count, { removedAtStart })`. Not `addRows()`.
- `repaint()` = values changed, same row count; `repaintHard()` = row count or heights changed; `updateCells()` = single cells.
- Variable row heights: implement `getRowHeight(i)`; `getConstantRowHeight()` only if all rows are equally high. `defaultRowHeights` only applies to models the factory builds or whose `getRowHeight()` returns 0.
- Save the column layout when the user resizes or moves a column: `onColumnResizeEnd` / `onColumnMoveEnd` (wrappers `columnResizeEnd`, `columnMoveEnd`, since 1.1.110) – once per drag, after the change; read `tableApi.getState(["columns"])` there. Lock a column: `ColumnDef.resizable: false`, `movable: false`. Double click on the column border fits the width (`columnAutoWidth`, `tableApi.autoResizeColumn(column)`).
- Empty table: the host div needs a fixed height and the stylesheet `@guiexpert/table/css/main.css`.

## Feature reference

What the table can do – one line per feature, details in instructions.md (each line names the options and API).

- Virtual scrolling for handling large datasets
- Excellent performance for large tables
- No third-party dependencies
- UI-agnostic design
- Column interactions (resize, reorder)
- Row sorting
- Row, column, and range selection
- Single and multi-selection
- Row and column spanning
- Fixed columns (left and right)
- Tree table (hierarchical view)
- Accessibility: WAI-ARIA grid/treegrid for screen readers (aria-rowcount/rowindex with virtual scrolling, aria-activedescendant focus, aria-sort, aria-selected, live-region announcements; options ariaLabel, ariaLabelledBy, ariaDescribedBy, ariaTexts; tableApi.announce()) and keyboard navigation (arrows, Home/End, Ctrl+Home/End, Page Up/Down, Enter, header focus) – since 1.1.91
- Overlays: "Loading…" with a CSS spinner (tableApi.showLoadingOverlay(text?), hideOverlay(), getOverlayState(); `loading` prop in all framework wrappers, no table re-creation) and automatic "No rows to show" / "No matching rows" (tableOptions.overlayOptions: texts, autoNoRows, blockInteractionWhileLoading, loadingDelayInMs, getOverlayElement; CSS variables --ge-table-overlay-*, --ge-table-spinner-*) – since 1.1.92
- Row numbers: TableFactory.createTableModel({ rows, rowNumbersVisible: true | { mode: "display" | "original", format, headerLabel, exported, minWidthInPx } }) or new RowNumberColumnDef() as first column; fixed left, width follows the largest number, role="rowheader", click selects the row, "#" selects all, not in copy/Excel unless exported; column indices shift by one – tableApi.getColumnIndex(property) – since 1.1.93
- Aggregation / total rows: TableFactory.createTableModel({ rows, columnDefs, footerAggregates: { total: "sum" } | [{ label, aggregates }] | { rows, labelProperty, rowHeight, source: "filtered" | "all", getRows } }) builds an AreaModelAggregateFooter (keys = column properties; aggregators "sum" | "count" | "avg" | "min" | "max" | "countDistinct" | "first" | "last" or own AggregatorIf { init, add, merge, result }; spec { aggregator, value: path | (row) => unknown, format }); follows filter and sorting, tree = filtered leaves, recomputed after filter/sort/edit/updateCells/tableApi.repaint() (AreaModelIf.invalidateDerivedValues?), never while scrolling; label cell role="rowheader"; Excel gets numbers. Helpers aggregate(rows, value, aggregator), aggregateColumns(rows, specs), Aggregators, formatAggregateValue. Selection: tableApi.getSelectionAggregates() → { count, numericCount, sum, avg, min, max, capped } (SelectionAggregator.maxCells) – since 1.1.94
- Row grouping: RowGroupFactory.createTableModel<T>({ rows, columnDefs, groupBy: ["region", (row) => key, { value, name, label, format, order: "asc" | "desc" | "insertion" | fn }], aggregations: { umsatz: "sum" }, footerAggregates?, groupColumn?: { headerLabel, width, showCount, label, fixed }, hideGroupedColumns?, expanded?: boolean | level | fn, emptyLabel? }) → body AreaModelRowGroups (a tree: isAreaModelTree true, isAreaModelRowGroups true) with a fixed RowGroupColumnDef ("Nord (3)"), grouped columns hidden, total row; group = merge of sub-group states (avg stays correct); externalFilterFunction gets the row objects, aggregates/counts follow the filter; sort by aggregate / group key, tableApi.sort(fn) sorts rows inside groups; edits recompute only the changed path (invalidateDerivedValues(change?: DerivedValuesChangeIf)), a changed grouped value moves the row; tableApi.setRowGroupBy(levels) / getRowGroupBy() regroup without a new model (expanded state by stable RowGroup.id kept); model: getGroups(), findGroup(path), getRowGroup(rowIndex), getDetailRow(rowIndex), getTotals(), getCheckedRows(), expandToLevel(n), setRows(), regroup(); engine without table: groupRows(rows, groupBy), aggregateRowGroups(groups, specs, accept?); isRowGroup, isGroupRow, isRowGroupColumnDef; CSS ge-table-row-group*, --ge-table-row-group-* – since 1.1.94
- Pivot tables: PivotFactory.createTableModel<T>({ rows, rowFields: RowGroupField[] (like groupBy), columnFields?: RowGroupField[], values: ("path" | fn | { value, aggregator?: "sum" (default) | "avg" | … | AggregatorIf, name?, label?, format? })[], subtotals?, columnSubtotals? (default: ≥ 2 column fields, collapsible column groups), totalColumn?: "fixed" (default) | true | false, totalRow?, maxColumns? (1000, more keys are cut off with a warning, totals still count all rows), expanded?, emptyLabel?, emptyText? (empty combination = undefined, not 0), totalLabel?, groupColumn?, valueColumnWidth?, rowNumbersVisible? }) → PivotTableModel (a TableModel) with body AreaModelPivot (a tree of RowGroup rows, isAreaModelTree true), header AreaModelCellGroups, footer AreaModelPivotFooter; subtotals/totals merged from aggregation states (avg correct); externalFilterFunction gets the source objects (filter before the aggregation), columns stay; sort by a value column / key; tableApi.setPivotConfig(changes, rows?) / getPivotConfig() pivot again without a new model; body: getResult() (PivotResult: rowGroups, columnGroups, columnLeaves, values, truncated, getValue(row?, column?, value?), getCount, getSourceRows), getColumnInfo(c), getColumnProperty(path, value?), getColumnIndex(path), getCellSourceRows(r, c), getRowGroup(r); engine without table: pivotRows(rows, config, accept?); isPivotTableModel, isAreaModelPivot, isPivotColumnDef; CSS ge-table-pivot-*, --ge-table-pivot-* – since 1.1.94
- Calculated columns, „Show values as“, formulas (since 1.1.95, body of object-array / tree / row-group models): ColumnDef.create({ property, valueGetter?: (row, ctx: ValueGetterContextIf { property, getValue(row, p), hasColumn(p), isCalculated(p), aggregate(p, aggregator) }) => unknown, valueSetter?: (row, value) => boolean | void (without it a calculated column is never editable), showValuesAs?: "percentOfColumnTotal" | "percentOfGrandTotal" | "percentOfParentTotal" | "percentOfRowTotal" | "differenceFromPrevious" | "runningTotal" | "rank" | { mode, fractionDigits?, format? }, formula?: "[price] * [quantity] * 1.19", formulaOptions?: { functions } }); one evaluation point (getValueByT) → sorting (memo per pass, errors last), copy, Excel, footerAggregates and RowGroupFactory aggregations/groupBy use computed values; filter: tableApi.getRowValue(row, property); reference of shares = filtered rows, sorting by raw value, Excel: shares as number with format 0.0% (ExcelFormattedValueIf { value, numberFormat }, ExcelService.supportsNumberFormats); pivot: values: [{ value, showValuesAs: "percentOfRowTotal" }] (4 percent modes, sorts by the share), AreaModelPivot.getShownValue(group, info); tableApi.setShowValuesAs(property, mode | undefined) / getShowValuesAs(property); formulas: compileFormula(source, { functions }?) → CompiledFormula { source, ast, error, fields, usesAggregates, evaluate(row, ctx?) } – Pratt parser + closures, no eval / new Function (CSP-safe), fields = own properties only ([constructor] → #NAME?), operators = <> < <= > >= & + - * / ^ (−2^2 = −4), TRUE/FALSE, texts "…"/'…', functions ROUND ABS FLOOR CEILING MOD SQRT POWER IF IFERROR AND OR NOT CONCAT LEN UPPER LOWER TRIM ISBLANK, SUM/AVG/AVERAGE/MIN/MAX/COUNT([field]) = column aggregate over the filtered rows (cached); errors FormulaError { code: "#ERROR!" | "#NAME?" | "#VALUE!" | "#DIV/0!" | "#NUM!" | "#CIRC!", message } (isFormulaError, CSS ge-table-cell-error, --ge-table-cell-error-color, tooltip = message), never thrown; createFormulaValueGetter, FORMULA_FUNCTION_NAMES; tableApi.setColumnFormula(property, source, options?) → FormulaError | undefined; helpers calculateShowValuesAs(values, mode), formatShowValuesAs(value, config), resolveShowValuesAs, isPercentShowValuesAs, sumOfNumbers, SHOW_VALUES_AS_MODES – no cell references (=B2), no formula editor UI
- Row drag (since 1.1.95): ColumnDef.rowDrag: true | (row, rowIndex) => boolean (drag handle in that column) or TableFactory.createTableModel({ rows, rowDrag: true }) (first data column); Pointer Events (mouse, touch, pen), threshold, ghost (text, never HTML), drop marker, auto-scroll at the body edges (quadratic, computed rows – works with virtual scrolling and capped scroll heights), Escape / pointercancel cancel; tableOptions.rowDragOptions: { managed: true (default; table moves the rows in place via the optional AreaModelIf.moveRows/canMoveRows – AreaModelObjectArray, AreaModelArrayOfArrays, AreaModelTree; blocked while a column is sorted asc/desc or a filter hides rows: handles dimmed, announcement) | false (only events, no blocking), multiRow (selected rows travel together), treeDropInside (tree: upper/lower quarter = sibling, middle = child; no cycles), dragThresholdInPx, autoScrollZoneInPx, autoScrollMaxSpeedInPx, ghostText(rows) }; events EventListenerIf.onRowDragStart/onRowDragMove/onRowDragEnd(GeRowDragEvent { type: "start" | "move" | "end" | "cancel", source: "pointer" | "keyboard", rows, rowIndices, target?: RowDropTargetIf { rowIndex, position: "before" | "after" | "inside" }, toIndex, outside, managed, moved, originalEvent, preventDefault() }), wrappers rowDragStart/rowDragMove/rowDragEnd; keyboard ActionId MOVE_ROW_UP/MOVE_ROW_DOWN (Ctrl+Alt+Up/Down, aria-keyshortcuts on the handle cell, announcement "Row moved to position 7 of 20"); tableApi.moveRows(rowIndices, target | index), isRowDragging(), cancelRowDrag(); helpers moveArrayItems, getInsertBeforeIndex, calcMoveToIndex, moveTreeRows, canMoveTreeRows; row grouping / pivot: managed not possible (use managed: false); CSS ge-table-row-drag-*, ge-table-row-drop-indicator, --ge-table-row-drag-* / --ge-table-row-drop-*
- Master/detail (since 1.1.97): tableOptions.masterDetail: { detailRenderer: (container, row, ctx: DetailRenderContextIf) => cleanup? | DetailRendererIf, detailHeight: number | "auto" (default, ResizeObserver) | (row, rowIndex) => …, estimatedDetailHeight (200), isMaster(row, rowIndex), toggleColumn (index | property, default: first data column behind row numbers/checkbox), maxRenderedDetails (50, LRU of hidden contents), getRowId } – only flat body models (tree/row groups/pivot: ignored + warning). Detail rows live in one layer div ge-table-detail-layer over the body (full width incl. fixed columns, does not scroll horizontally, never cleared by the virtual rendering); heights are extras of the body RowLayout (prefix sums, also for variable row heights: O(log n) per frame). Content created when first visible, hidden (content-visibility) when scrolled out – state and scroll positions stay –, destroyed on collapse, LRU, refreshDetail, destroy (cleanup fn, ctx.signal aborted, nested tables destroyed). ctx: row, rowIndex, tableApi, recreated, signal, createTable({ tableModel, tableOptions?, eventListener?, height? }) → TableApi of a nested table. Keyed by row object or getRowId (survives sort/filter/setRows). API: setDetailExpanded(rowIndex | row, expanded), toggleDetail, isDetailExpanded, getExpandedDetailRows, expandAllDetails / collapseAllDetails (no event per row), refreshDetail, getDetailElement; getBodyRowTop / getBodyRowIndexAtY on the scope. Events EventListenerIf.onDetailExpandedChanged(GeDetailEvent { row, rowIndex, expanded, source: "mouse" | "keyboard" | "api" | "state" }), wrappers detailExpandedChanged; events from a detail row are ignored by the outer table; mouse wheel over a detail scrolls the outer table if nothing inside scrolls. ARIA: host role treegrid, master rows aria-expanded, detail rows role row + gridcell aria-colspan in an own rowgroup (aria-owns); Enter toggles, Tab enters the detail, Shift+Tab back. State part "details" (detailRowIds, autoRestoreDetailState). Copy/Excel without details. Framework detail components: DetailComponentRendererWrapper (React, Preact, Vue, Svelte 4/5, Solid; props row, rowIndex, tableApi, context), Angular DetailRenderWrapperFactory + DetailComponentRendererIf.setDetail(row, ctx). CSS ge-table-detail-*, --ge-table-detail-bg/-border/-toggle-color/-toggle-hover-bg
- Right-to-left (since 1.1.98): tableOptions.direction: "ltr" (default) | "rtl" | "auto" (getComputedStyle(host).direction before the table sets dir; read once when built – new options object = rebuild). The host gets dir="rtl"/"ltr" (restored by destroy()). All positions are computed from the start of the row; ConvenienceDomService.setDirection("rtl") writes them as CSS right instead of left → the whole table is mirrored. "left"/"right" in API names mean start/end: fixedLeftColumnCount = start (right in RTL), fixedRightColumnCount = end, NAVIGATE_LEFT = backwards, FillDirection "right" = forwards, ge-table-text-align-left/-right = start/end (new: -start/-end). Positions count from the start: scrollToPixel(x, y), GeScrollEvent.scrollLeft, state scroll.left (≥ 0); browser scrollLeft is 0…negative in RTL → tableScope.getViewportScrollLeft()/setViewportScrollLeft(x), helpers getLogicalScrollLeft, setLogicalScrollLeft, toPhysicalScrollLeft, canScrollHorizontally, toLogicalX, resolveTableDirection, mirrorArrowKeys. Keyboard: ←/→ swapped before the shortcut mapping is looked up. Resize handle at the left edge (dragging left widens). Excel: ExcelExportOptionsIf { rightToLeft } (4th parameter of ExcelService.downloadExcel / 3rd of createExcelBlob), set by tableApi.downloadExcel for RTL tables. CSS on logical properties (padding-inline-start, text-align: start) – pixel-identical in LTR; RTL-only rules .ge-table[dir="rtl"] (expanded tree arrow, detail toggle, pending marker). Nested master/detail tables inherit the direction. api.getDirection(): "ltr" | "rtl"
- Fill handle and batch edit (since 1.1.96): tableOptions.fillHandle: true | { direction: "both" | "vertical" | "horizontal", fillValue(ctx: FillValueContextIf) => unknown (undefined = default), maxCells (100000), dragThresholdInPx, autoScrollZoneInPx, autoScrollMaxSpeedInPx } – square at the bottom right corner of the last range of a SelectionModel("range"), Pointer Events, preview, auto-scroll, Escape; series rules computeFillValues(sourceValues, count, backward?, mode: "auto" | "alternate" | "copy"): one number copied, several numbers linear (uneven: best-fit line), dates +1 day or +n months (month ends stay; Date stays Date, ISO text stays text), "Item 9" → "Item 10" (leading zeros kept), others repeat; ⌥/Alt (or Ctrl) switches series/copy; computeFillChanges / getFillRange; only editable cells of shown columns (calculated columns need valueSetter), editInputPipe + ColumnDef.validate(value, row) => message; keyboard ActionId FILL_DOWN (Ctrl/⌘+D) / FILL_RIGHT (Ctrl/⌘+R), consumed only with fillHandle and a selected range; tableApi.fillRange(source: CellRange, direction, count, mode?), isFilling(), cancelFill(). Batch edit: tableOptions.batchEdit: true | { blockCommitOnInvalid } (always on) or tableApi.startBatchEdit(); values are shown (class ge-table-cell-pending, invalid ge-table-cell-invalid + aria-invalid + title) but not written; keyed by row object + property (sorting/filtering keep them), back to the original = no change; sorting/filter/totals/copy/Excel use written data; tableApi.getPendingChanges(): CellChangeIf[] { row, rowIndex (-1 = filtered out), columnIndex, property, oldValue, newValue, error? }, hasPendingChanges(), isBatchEditing(), commitBatchEdit(): boolean (false while invalid), cancelBatchEdit(); EventListenerIf.onBatchEditChanged(GeBatchEditEvent { type: "start" | "change" | "commit" | "cancel", changes, pendingCount, invalidCount, pendingChanges }), wrappers batchEditChanged. One write path tableApi.applyCellChanges([{ rowIndex, column: index | property, value }], source?) → CellChangeIf[]; onModelChanged once per edit / fill / commit with GeModelChangeEvent.changes + source ("edit" | "fill" | "commit" | "api"). CSS ge-table-fill-handle, ge-table-fill-preview, --ge-table-fill-*, --ge-table-cell-pending-*, --ge-table-cell-invalid-*. Paste: tableOptions.clipboard, undo: tableOptions.undo (since 1.1.99).
- Excel-style editing (since 1.1.99): tableOptions.editing: true | { startOnType, enterKey: "edit" | "moveDown", enterMoves, tabMoves, arrowKeysCommit, clearKeys, ctrlEnterFillsSelection, emptyValue, defaultEditable, maxClearCells } – type to overwrite, F2, Enter/Tab move, Escape cancels, Delete clears (source "clear"), Ctrl+Enter fills the selection, Ctrl+arrow to the data edge, Shift+arrow extends; one editor container in the host (CellEditorService), ColumnDef.editor "text" | "number" | "date" | factory, IME. api.startEditing/stopEditing/isEditing/getEditingCell/clearCells, api.subscribe(listener) → unsubscribe, event onEditingChanged (GeEditEvent).
- Clipboard (since 1.1.99): tableOptions.clipboard: true | { copyHeaders, copyValue: "text" | "raw", html, pasteAddsRows, createRow, maxPasteCells, processCopy, processPaste } – Ctrl+C/X/V via the browser's copy/cut/paste events, TSV + HTML table (Excel quoting), a single value fills the selection, only editable cells, editInputPipe + validate; cut = one operation (sources "paste", "cut"). api.copySelection(), cutSelection(), pasteText(text), getSelectionAsText(), cancelCut(). Input pipes: sheetInputPipe(locale), createNumberInputPipe, createDateInputPipe, booleanInputPipe.
- Undo/redo (since 1.1.99): tableOptions.undo: true | { maxSteps, maxCells, onConflict: "skip" | "overwrite", recordApiChanges } – Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y (Cmd+Shift+Z) for edit, fill, paste, cut, clear, batch edits and structure changes; rows found by object (sorting/filter safe). api.undo(), redo(), canUndo(), canRedo(), clearUndoHistory(), getUndoState(), batchUndoable(label, fn); event onUndoStackChanged (GeUndoEvent: canUndo, canRedo, undoLabel, redoLabel).
- Cell formulas with A1 references (since 1.1.99): tableOptions.cellFormulas: true | { columns, functions } (ColumnDef.cellFormulas: false = free text) – texts with "=" in the data are formulas ("'=" = text): A1, $A$1, B2:D9, A:A, 70 Excel functions (FORMULA_FUNCTION_INFO; SUM, AVERAGE, IF, IFS, VLOOKUP, XLOOKUP, INDEX/MATCH, SUMIFS, COUNTIFS, TEXT, DATE, EOMONTH …), errors #DIV/0! #REF! #NAME? #VALUE! #N/A #NUM! #CIRC!; dependency graph, only dependents recalculate; own parser, no eval. Formula input: colored references, pointing with arrows/mouse, F4 toggles $, function list (combobox) and hint. Fill/copy shift relative references; Excel export with real formulas: downloadExcel(name, author, { cellFormulas: true }). api.getCellInput/getCellValue/setCellInput/getCellAddress/getCellByAddress/evaluateFormula/getPrecedents/getDependents/recalculate/getSheetEngine. DOM-free: SheetEngine.fromArrays(data), shiftFormula, adjustFormula.
- Spreadsheet mode (since 1.1.99): SpreadsheetFactory.create({ data: unknown[][], rowCount (100), columnCount (26), columnWidth, rowHeight, rowNumbers, locale, functions, tableOptions }) → { tableModel: SpreadsheetTableModel, tableOptions } – column letters (AreaModelSheetHeader), row numbers, sparse AreaModelSheet; preset tableOptions.spreadsheet: true | { editing, clipboard, undo, cellFormulas, fillHandle } (false = off) for any flat table (TableFactory columnLetters: true). FormulaBar(container, api) – address box + formula input. api.getActiveCell(), goToAddress("B2:C5"), insertRows(at, count), deleteRows, insertColumns, deleteColumns (references adjusted, one undo step, source "structure"), getSheetData() (inputs for JSON).
- Angular signal component (since 1.1.100, Angular 22 and later): TableSignalComponent, selector guiexpert-table-signal, from @guiexpert/angular-table@22.x – inputs (input()) tableModel (TableModelIf | undefined), tableOptions (default new TableOptions()), loading, debounceMouseClickDelay (150, 0 = synchronous); tableApi = model<TableApi | undefined>() → [(tableApi)]="api" with api = signal<TableApi | undefined>(undefined), (tableApiChange), viewChild(TableSignalComponent)?.tableApi(); set when the table is built, switches directly to the new API on a new model/options, undefined after destroy, written from outside = replaced. Outputs (output()): no tableReady (the API comes as the signal tableApi / tableApiChange), mouseClicked, mouseMoved, mouseDragging, mouseDraggingEnded, contextMenu (camelCase – TableComponent's (contextmenu) also receives the native MouseEvent first), scroll, modelChanged, selectionChanged, focusChanged, checkboxChanged, stateChanged, rowDragStart/Move/End, batchEditChanged, detailExpandedChanged, editingChanged, undoStackChanged, columnResizeStart/End, columnMoveStart/End (since 1.1.110) – events of the table (mouse, keyboard, scroll …) are emitted outside the Angular zone (write signals in handlers). effect() instead of ngOnChanges, no RxJS, zoneless (provideZonelessChangeDetection()), SSR: no table on the server. TableComponent (<guiexpert-table>) unchanged for Angular 14 – 22+.
- Column drag (since 1.1.110): events EventListenerIf.onColumnResizeStart/End (GeColumnResizeEvent: type "start" | "end" | "cancel", source "mouse" | "dblclick", columnIndex, columnDef, property, oldWidth, newWidth) and onColumnMoveStart/End (GeColumnMoveEvent: type, fromIndex, toIndex, columnDef, property, columnOrder, moved) – only user actions, once per drag, the end after the change, start after 4 px, Escape / tableApi.cancelColumnDrag() = "cancel", tableApi.isColumnDragging(); wrappers columnResizeStart/End, columnMoveStart/End. Locks: ColumnDef.resizable: false (no handle, no double click, no auto width), movable: false (fixed place, applyState keeps it); RowNumberColumnDef has both false; a column stays in its area (west/center/east). Double click on the resize handle fits the width (no sorting): tableOptions.columnAutoWidth: { doubleClick (true), maxRows (10,000: all body rows, above only the rendered rows), getWidth(ctx: ColumnAutoWidthContextIf { columnIndex, columnDef, property, source, firstRenderedRow, lastRenderedRow, measureText(text), getDefaultWidth() }) => number | undefined }, limited by minWidth/maxWidth; tableApi.autoResizeColumn(index | property | ColumnDef) → width | undefined.
- Live data / log tail (since 1.1.108): tableApi.appendRows(rows, { follow?: "auto" (default: stays at the end if it was at the end, else the first visible row stays) | true (always the end) | false (freeze), maxRows?: ring buffer – oldest rows removed from the start in blocks of ≥ 1 % }) → AppendRowsResultIf { added, shown, removed, following } | false (tree, row groups, pivot, spreadsheet, cell formulas) – AreaModelObjectArray body only, IN PLACE (pushes to your array, no copy), O(k): externalFilterFunction only for the new rows, sorted column / sort(fn) → merged in (binary search, behind equal rows); selection, focus, Shift+arrow anchor and checked rows stay at their rows (RowIndexShift, SelectionModel/FocusModel.adjustForRowChanges – no onSelectionChanged unless a selected row left the buffer); one render pass, none when only rows below the view came in (cells not rebuilt). Held mouse button: "auto" keeps the rows under the pointer and follows again after release. Own AreaModel: append yourself, then tableApi.rowsAppended(count, { follow, removedAtStart }). Not addRows() (copies all rows, resets filter and sort). Showcase logtail, demo apps/table-demo/log-tail.html, LogTailController + createLogTailModelAndOptions in @guiexpert/demo-table-models.
- Custom filtering
- In-place cell editing
- User-defined key and mouse events
- Customizable look and feel via CSS variables
- State persistence: column layout (width, order, visibility), sorting, scroll position, expanded tree nodes, checked and selected rows, header groups, custom data – in localStorage (tableOptions.autoRestoreOptions: autoRestoreColumnLayout, autoRestoreSortingState, autoRestoreScrollPosition, autoRestoreCollapsedExpandedState, autoRestoreCheckedState, autoRestoreSelectedState, autoRestoreHeaderGroupState, autoRestoreCustomState; storage: StateStorageIf) or on your server (tableApi.getState(parts?), applyState(state, parts?), resetState(), setCustomState(), tableOptions.initialState, EventListenerIf.onStateChanged(GeStateChangeEvent), `stateChanged` event in all wrappers); columns by property, rows by getRowId – since 1.1.92
- Customizable cell contents via renderers

## Documentation and links

- Developer guide (all frameworks, checked against the code): https://github.com/guiexperttable/mono/blob/main/instructions.md
- Angular guide (14–22, signals): https://github.com/guiexperttable/mono/blob/main/packages/angular-table/instructions.md
- API reference (TypeDoc): https://gui.expert/api
- Training (40 chapters, step by step, live demos): https://gui.expert/training/
- What's new (features since October 2026 with code): https://gui.expert/whats-new/
- Showcases: https://gui.expert/showcase/ (large, logtail, crypto, treetable, pivot, spreadsheet, masterdetail, rtl …)
- Demos in the repo: apps/table-demo (plain TS), apps/*-table-demo (frameworks), apps/angular-table-demo

## Notes for LLMs

- Prefer the recipes above; for anything else read instructions.md (it is compiled against the code) – the code wins.
- Do not invent APIs (see the last pitfall); if a feature is listed as "not built in" (R17), say so and show the way
  with the existing API.
- Plain TypeScript works in every framework; the wrappers only add props/events and lifecycle.
- License: MIT for current releases ("free, also for commercial use"); do not quote prices.
